source.title: Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt
source.authors: Tamay Besiroglu; Ege Erdil; M. Barnett; J. You

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly attempts to replicate Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 3, fitting the same parametric loss function to reconstructed data and comparing the resulting compute-optimal policy.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites results from Hoffmann et al.'s Approaches 1 and 2 and other studies; those cited findings are not recorded as rows. The authors' own reconstructed-data fits, fit comparisons, and derived policies are recorded.
record.test_reason: The study refits Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 3 parametric loss L(N,D)=E+A/N^α+B/D^β with Huber loss on 240 points reconstructed from Hoffmann et al.'s Figure 4. It then derives the compute-optimal split, so it is a same-method replication. It also argues the original Approach 3 estimates are wrong, a T5 element. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with three refinements. First, most of the poor fit comes from rounding the published parameters, especially β. Second, the remaining significant gap and the implausibly narrow CIs come from early optimizer termination: Hoffmann et al. averaged rather than summed the Huber loss. Third, the authors' converged refit gives a≈0.51 and about 20 tokens/parameter, consistent with Approaches 1–2 and Chinchilla. They also stress large residual uncertainty: 4–40 tokens/parameter at ≥1e26 FLOP.
record.recipe_differences: The paper replicates Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 3 using the same parametric loss form and Huber fitting approach, but reconstructs a subset of the data from Figure 4 rather than using the original dataset. It uses BFGS rather than L-BFGS and reports differences in initialization and loss aggregation.
record.method_sensitivity: The fit changes with parameter rounding and optimizer behavior; inclusion of five low-token-per-parameter outliers increases parameter uncertainty.
record.problems: The dataset is reconstructed from a plot rather than the original run-level data. The authors note uncertainty from y-coordinate extraction and color-to-loss mapping, with color precision of approximately 0.01. Their reconstructed dataset has 240 points, compared with Hoffmann et al.'s reported over 400 observations; five points are difficult to fit and excluded from main parameter estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No material results bearing on the tested versions were left out. Additional bootstrap and likelihood-test details are discussed in Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix A.1–A.2.

untested.parts: Only the N and D axes within about 70M–16B parameters and 5B–500B tokens are covered. There is no compute-axis law and no range beyond the original data.
Entire version: no held-out larger runs are predicted.
The Kaplan-style allocation is not tested. There are no new training runs, and the split is not verified at large compute.

Not tested: parameter counting, training schedule, and data-quality choices, and curves bending away from a single power law in general. Tested: rounding, optimizer convergence/loss aggregation, and outlier inclusion.

missing.what: χ² test of parameter equality with unrounded Hoffmann values: p<1e-51 (<1e-48 in another statement), and p<1e-35 with outliers in Σ. Individual parameter tests: E p=2.6e-6, β p=1.1e-4; A, B and α are not significantly different.
Main-fit policy of about 20 tokens per parameter, as distinct from the outlier-included 25.6.
Likelihood-ratio p<10^-235 for the rounded Hoffmann fit, which conflicts with Table 2's 1.22e-16.

record.verdict_notes: Data are digitized from a plot (loss precision about 0.01) and cover 240 of more than 400 original runs. Rows r2 and r4 duplicate each other. The record's V3 'challenges' label from r8 is not justified: the 70 tokens/parameter figure reflects a mis-fit, not evidence about the true allocation.

versions.untested_parts: The study examines a reconstructed subset of Hoffmann et al.'s data and a parametric loss function in model size and training tokens. It does not independently test loss scaling with compute while varying the other factors, or establish the law across all settings and orders of magnitude.
The study does not hold out larger runs and test predictions from fits to smaller runs.
It tests policies derived from the fitted loss function on reconstructed data; it does not run new training experiments across compute budgets.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer are not tested.

The study identifies sensitivity to parameter rounding and optimization procedure and compares fitted policies. It does not test every listed setup choice or establish that curves bend away from a single power law generally.

rows.subject: Optimal scaling policy derived from Hoffmann et al.'s Approach 3 estimates
rows.stage_stated: compute-optimal training policy inferred from reported pre-training loss fit
rows.operation_detail: Derive the compute-optimal allocation from Hoffmann et al.'s fitted parameters
rows.baseline: 20 tokens per parameter used for Chinchilla
rows.uncertainty: The paper describes the confidence intervals as extremely narrow; exact policy interval values are shown in Figure 5
rows.note: The authors say this prescription is inconsistent with the ratio used for Chinchilla and with Approaches 1 and 2.
